Absolutely beautiful game. Very responsive controls. I initially just wanted to see if it would run on my low-end laptop. And I ended up getting completely absorbed in it for three hours. Highly recommended.

Really enjoyed this game. Definitely feels like old-school zelda mixed with 2d souls. My only issue with the game came from some hitboxes either lingering or feeling slightly off, but you get used to it after awhile. Also didn't like how, when using the World Map, it looks like the game dips to 10fps while you scroll. Honestly, these are minor issues in an otherwise wonderful game.

Edit: Literally one day after I posted this review, a patch came out addressing both the map frame rate issue and the hitboxes. I honestly have no complaints now, for me, this game is perfect.

We need more Lovecraftian horror cowboy games. We really do. I enjoyed the story. It was a tight experience. The soundtrack was pretty good. The art style isn't really my cup of tea but I still enjoyed it. I mean I sunk 18 hours into the game writing this review so I guess you can say the art style is rubbing off on me.

The gameplay has a lot going for itself in terms of combat. You have melee, guns, magic, and thowables. I'm not big into magic personally but it has a lot of play. I like going in with the shovel and Conquistador's Axe for melee. Ivory pistol for long range. Cluster and fire grenades along with dynamite really pay off. Shooting can feel a bit finicky. I don't know if its me or my PS4 controller. The hook caster can be used to bring in enemies into melee range.

The level design is great but its unfortuinate there isn't a local map option or a more guiding indication of where to proceed. Finding Kansas Stilton was a pain but not frustrating.

The boss fights were phenominal. I feel accomplished beating the main story bosses and some of the optional ones without using a guide. They can be frustrating but like always its just a matter of determining the pattern of combat. Challenging but not ridiculously so.

All in all I recommend Tombwater. I still have more to explore and unlock as well as other play styles to try.

I can't give this game a high enough rating. It's the most fun I've had on a playthrough in the last year, and I went further out of my way to search out every last corner of it than almost any game in recent memory. I never would have expected that an Eldrich horror motif held against a moody western backdrop in a Zelda-like envelope would work, but it absolutely did---and every time I put it down, I was racing back to play again. 

What's so good about it?

Art, thematics and atmosphere. As a trade-off for the lack of guidance, the world you're dropped into has a genuinely forlorn 19th century mining town feel to it. So, when the horror elements begin, the sense of isolation and survival is very immersive. This is all backed up by a simple and authentic-feeling musical score that never insists on itself, yet keeps the vibe and pacing on point. 

Deeply satisfying exploration. Tombwater's map is absolutely massive, and there is a TON of stuff to find in every direction. Every tiny secret you find has a reward at the end of it, and your options for combat and optimization expand geometrically as a result. 

Combat and specialization. You have melee weapons, three types of ranged guns, spells, throwables and explosives. You can then optimize any of them with a charm system, which can then also be further boosted by refillable nostrums (potions). The crafting system is very dynamic, allowing you to disassemble any item you craft for a full refund on your materials, which allows you to experiment with different options for a time, then return to a table and try something else rather than commit permanently to something you may not ultimately like. Despite the plethora of occult spells, I happened to decide (which turned out to be the right move) that I wanted to focus on explosives. While my late-game power level did ultimately trivialize most boss fights, it was insanely fun. (NOTE: I have read in the Discussions that the devs may patch a nerf to explosives damage. Womp. Oh well, got my fun while it lasted). 

No douchey design elements, like boss run backs, horizontal "upgrades," or another fekkin' parry system. You all know what I'm talking about. Glad to see devs starting to listen to players who prefer FUN over masochism. 

Minor feedback:

In-game menu. There's decent tracking of equipment, events and NPCs, though I would love to see a location-based percent completion tracker offered at endgame, as some of those "Collect all XX" achievements feel near impossible with a map that size. 

There were a few small bugs I encountered as I played, like certain bosses double spawning an inert second copy of themselves, or inadvertently getting no-clipped out of bounds by changing screens a few times. 

The in-game map is about as useful as a Braille keypad on a drive-up ATM. Hat tip to Demajen. 

The difficulty curve is a bit backwards. Early game deaths felt instantaneous and every encounter frantic. For example, the Lamplighter boss took countless tries, and almost no strategy seemed to make it easier. By mid game, there were almost no deaths that weren't due to carelessness or rushing, which could be corrected with very minor adjustments. The last 5-6 area bosses (other than the true ending) were first-try plow-throughs. 

--

All in all, this game is glorious, and I strongly recommend it to anyone who might appreciate a true MV/ZL masterclass. I will definitely be starting my second playthrough very soon.

I went in expecting Tombwater to be a zelda-like with Bloodborne and Wild West elements and it kinda isn't that. It LOOKS like a Zelda-like, and some of its systems are simplistic like a Zelda-like — thanks to the fact that it is built on the Solarus engine, which is responsible for a lot of LttP-style fan games — but it doesn't really *feel* like one.

After six or seven hours of the game, I still couldn't put my finger on the growing discordance in my brain between what I thought the game should be and what it actually was, so I went into the gameplay options and played around with the damage scaling. 

Doubling the damage we did while halving the damage we took (there are more granular options than these) really helped swing the game mentally back to where I wanted it to be, and from there I tweaked them at my leisure as I played through the rest of this rather large game.

There's a lot to like here. The pixel art is great, the world is large, the music is wonderful.

There's also some things that are a bit iffy. You *will* get the fall-in-pits animation when you've clearly made it onto land; you will sometimes need to pixel perfect length your dash in order to avoid hazards; and some of the enemies can absolutely massacre your health with multihits (even with the reduced damage multiplier turned all the way).

The game's biggest issue, however, is its map. It is woefully inadequate for a game of this size and complexity. While the biggest offender is the Central District, the game's "hub" area for want of a better phrase, navigating around the game world — both inside and outside of the almost dungeon-like areas — is not really helped in the slightest by the in-game map, which shows a vague sketch overworld with random buildings drawn on rather than actual street layouts.

The game is tagged as a metroidvania, features metroidvania-style tools, but doesn't in any way have a metroidvania-style map. And if there's one complaint I've seen from people both on the game's discord and elsewhere, it's that the map is bad.

I mean, I spent 60+ hours making my own map guide for the game simply because I just COULD NOT get around the place. I didn't know it was going to take that long, admittedly, and the game itself certainly isn't that long. I finished it in around 20 hours after the difficulty tweaks.

Thing is, I'm not entirely sure what I would do to tune up the map to something better. A classic Zelda-style game is based on a grid system, and Tombwater just isn't put together like that. It's especially noticeable in some of the interior areas which just don't line up properly in an F1 F2 F3 type manner. And, to be honest, the devs have gotten around this problem by not giving maps for any interior areas at all.

I don't want to of flog the proverbial horse here — there are multiple poor dead horses collecting flies in this eldritch wild west setting anyways — but I just want people to be aware of what they're getting into. Tombwater is a REALLY good game, but unless you have the spatial awareness and navigational ability of some kind of eldritch god, you're probably going to get lost quite a bit.

这是我今年第二个想要打差评的独立游戏，总体来说：
[h1]非常不推荐半价以上购买[/h1]



[h2]优点[/h2]
1.非常大的地图，连接点很多，四通八达
2.武器、法术、装备、道具十分多样
3.剧情和立绘也不错

[h2]缺点[/h2]
1.糟糕的地图设计（按"M"的显示的那个）。
（1）我不理解为什么近期某些 类银河战士恶魔城 都喜欢在地图上恶心你。我就想问了这地图除了让你知道自己在哪个区域以外，还有什么用。打标记的作用也几乎为零。做的很敷衍。

2.糟糕的战斗系统。
（1）明明射击能够360°全方向，但是近战只有WASD四个方向，法术也只有八个方向。这难道是什么无法解决的技术问题，还是单纯刁难玩家？
（2）极长的前后摇，除了 匕首类 武器，其他都有 1s 的前摇，冲刺取消硬直也不是很流畅。法术施放更是缓慢。
很多独立游戏都有明显的误区，并不是疯狂削弱角色性能，就是 [b]类魂[/b]

3.烦人的怪物设计：
（1）这个和第二点是有关联的，所有敌人的攻击几乎是瞬发的，并且是360°全方向。而你却有将近 1s 的硬直，和受限的攻击方向，这非常的SUCK。
（2）同时，怪物的移动和位移非常快。

4.崩坏的数值设计：
（1）你能在前期获得Sculpture Garden这个能够用到中后期的法术。同时，你也能在游戏中后期获得很多意义不明，强度甚至前期也不够用的法术。
（2）又比如Drainfield这种无限叠加的吸血陷阱
（3）有些近战武器和远程武器也有点搞笑，Harpoon Gun这种2格耗弹量，伤害不如1格耗弹量Carbine有存在必要吗，仅仅是为了穿透性？
还有Connon这种6格耗弹量，伤害仍然没有2发Carbine高的，你真的需要它的范围爆炸吗？

5.奇怪的传送系统：
（1）我直到游戏进度将近60%，仍然没有解锁传送系统，因为你不只需要解锁传送点，还需要在游戏中后期解锁传送能力。
这真的有什么意义吗？

6.此外，游戏经常有卡顿和掉帧，不清楚是游戏原因还是电脑原因，但我这个配置应该不至于是电脑原因

7.更迷惑的是，游戏里明明有根据鼠标方向近战攻击。怎么到了法术、钩锁还是只能通过控制WASD
攻击方向

I ran into some bugs early on, including crashes that cost me about three hours of progress. To be fair, I started playing right at launch, so it wasn’t too surprising. The good news is I’d learned enough by then to get back to where I was within an hour. Since that point, I’ve played through most of the game and had a much smoother experience.

I reached one ending and wasn’t sure if there were multiple, but thankfully the game let me reload a save from before the finale and keep going. I’m hoping they add a New Game Plus mode, because replaying without certain charms feels limiting, and it would be great to see the difficulty scale with each run.

The game is generally pretty challenging, though I was a bit let down by the final boss. At around level 50, it only took me a couple of tries, and I expected something more complex, like multiple phases. That said, it might be tied to not unlocking what seems like the “true” ending.

One big frustration was the large, tanky enemies in the mines. I spent 20–30 minutes carefully kiting and killing one, only to get almost no XP, which felt really unrewarding—especially when there are tons of them.

Overall, despite some rough edges, I really enjoyed the game and would definitely recommend it. I’m looking forward to future updates, possible DLC, and hopefully more features like New Game Plus as the game continues to grow.

Genuinely one of the best soulslike games I have ever played and one of the best games I have played in the last year. I highly recommend it for anyone who thinks the game looks even vaguely interesting. 

The balance between your gun being easier to use but having limited ammo and melee attacks restoring ammo leads to a very fun combat loop of shooting someone, running in for a couple of hits, then backing off to shoot them again. Along with spells running on a recharging resource makes you use your whole kit if you decide to run magic. 

Tombwater also has a much better directioning than most soulslikes thanks to the best guy, Amos. Amos can direct you where to go for your next main story objective and does it in a great way of just telling you the next location and rough directions to wherever you need to go next in a way that sounds natural for someone who has lived in a town for years. All sidequests tend to be easier to understand where they are going too. Either because they say where they intend to go, stay where they were, or go somewhere you know they are associated.

Weapon variety is very nice. Some are obviously just bigger weapon hit harder and swing slower but a good number have unique effects either through hit effects like lifedrain, tippers, or extra bullets on hit, or weapon arts that either aoe or buff. Guns meanwhile tend to have either reload speed, damage, or bonus effects such as pierce, AoE, or elemental effects.

Exploration is a main tenant and I think it does it wonderfully. Lots of shortcuts and side paths generally containing a new weapon, a flask upgrade, or a crafting material. It also takes a fair bit from Metroidvanias of "Hey here's a new ability! Remember that thing you saw earlier? Yeah you can go ahead and see what is there!" which I appreciate even if my memory is a bit rough. Luckily for the forgetful the game also has a map that lets you set custom markers. So you can mark something you can't do yet and come back for it later.

Crafting is done better than any other souls game that I can remember. Better than Elden Ring too for one sole reason. If you craft a bomb or something and use it, you get it back on rest. Thank you! It's still consumable until you rest at the campfires but instead of being  something that is used once and gone, it can now be an integral piece of your strategy. And you can uncraft something to get back the materials and use make something else instead which is beautiful. Make a poison bomb but decide you want a frost bomb instead? Uncraft and make the frost bomb with the materials.

The story is also nice. Simple to understand the surface elements with a fair bit of deeper info to delve into.

Overall, buy the game. I am shilling for this as I absolutely loved it start to finish. It is worth the price and then some.

I was on the fence about purchasing this game, according to my Steam Library I last played the demo in August of last year. The demo left a lot to be desired, and at the time did not seem to include features that would be integral to the final game. I don't believe you could even level up in the demo version(as of August 3, 2025). I will say, in my opinion, the demo does not do this game justice.

The final game is vastly improved, and being able to level up helps a bit to tune the difficulty level of the game. If you are struggling, you can increase your health and stamina by leveling to soak more damage and dodge more. The big problem with the demo, I believe, is the portion of the game taking place in the demo was on the more difficult side and also contained very limited options to upgrade your spells and equipment. The demo area also contained numerous exploding environmental hazards(TNT Barrels) and most of the enemies in the demo explode on death. The focus here is this: the demo made me wary of purchasing the full game, rather than be excited for the full release. However, I could still see the potential under the bits that made me frustrated.

At first, and remember my opinion was shaded by what I perceive as a less-than-stellar demo, the price for this game felt too high. I could not have been more wrong. This game is one of the best purchases I have made on Steam in 2026, and is definitely worth the price even after the introductory sale is over. I'm having tons of fun, even if I sometimes get stuck on the exploration bits or die repeatedly to a boss I shouldn't have.

And so, I will say it again: This is a really great game and I encourage everyone to purchase it.

The map feels massive and I will admit pre-fast travel going around and navigating through places is a bit of a chore but once you start to unlock more things and shortcuts and whatnot it really ramps up.

I really enjoyed this game. If it looks like something you will like, get it. Be warned that this game is a huge maze with a very vague map so if getting lost and trying to figure out where to go is not your cup of tea, approach with caution.

++ Solid combat
++ Chock full of content
-- Story is unoriginal and unsoulslike
- Did not like the map
I've been have a blast on this game so far. It's been really been scratching that Metroidvania itch!
Really diggin it so far!
Awesome game!

TL;DR: achei a mecânica de combate pouco fluida e, em boa parte, bem frustrante - por isso não recomendo. Ainda assim, vou tentar terminar o jogo. Ainda quero saber o que aconteceu com o Xerife.

Eu achei o combate meio injusto e pouco fluido. Seu personagem só consegue atacar corpo a corpo na direção que está olhando, limitado às quatro direções básicas (cima, baixo, esquerda e direita). Enquanto isso, a maioria dos inimigos - principalmente chefes - tem ataques em 360° e muitas vezes com área de efeito.

O ataque à distância até cobre 360°, mas depende de carregar com golpes corpo a corpo - o que acaba voltando ao problema da limitação do ângulo de ataque.

Somando isso aos ataques em área dos inimigos, à limitação de estamina, à demora na animação dos ataques e ao fato de o ataque ser direcionado pelo WASD, várias lutas acabam virando só correr ou ficar esquivando, esperando uma chance de atacar.

E mesmo quando essa chance aparece, muitas vezes o inimigo ataca antes, cancela sua animação e encaixa um combo. Cada golpe tira uma parte grande da vida (tipo 1/5, mesmo eu já estando com 30 pontos no atributo de vida) e ainda te impede de esquivar enquanto está tomando dano.

Além disso, a brecha para acertar os inimigos quase sempre é menor do que o tempo necessário para se reposicionar e iniciar a animação de ataque corpo a corpo.

Até agora, a melhor arma melee que encontrei foi o chicote. Por ter um alcance maior, ele permite manter uma distância mais segura, acertar o inimigo e sair da linha do próximo ataque com mais consistência.

Um glitch que encontrei por acaso: 
[spoiler] Em algumas situações, a recuperação da alma chegava a dar EXP suficiente para subir um ou mais níveis. Depois de morrer umas 15 vezes em uma boss fight e finalmente vencer, percebi que subi 17 níveis de tanto recuperar a alma. Não sei dizer o critério para replicar, mas parece funcionar com o dinheiro também se usar a Ghost Seed depois de já ter recuperado a alma. O item replica a mesma quantidade de dinheiro e EXP perdido na última alma - então se morrer com $1000, ele vai gerar uma alma com outros $1000 a cada uso.[/spoiler]

reviews.review: Liked the demos, Loved the final product. Cant wait to play more
its a really fun game with a lot of cool bosses and beasts, the map is useless though

Sometimes, a game will combine a bunch of things you love and it turns into a hot mess and you realize why no one did it before. 
Tombwater is not that. 
Old west setting, Link to the past style world traversal and combat, and a Bloodborne Story. 
these things are all awesome but you wouldn't think they'd work well together, but Tombwater pulls it off.
the world has a sense of mystery that just makes you want to explore every nook and cranny, something big budget games have been failing at for years with overly bloated open world maps. the combat is simple enough that it never becomes a mess of systems, but its challenging enough that you cant just flail your weapons at your problem until it dies. the balance between melee and gunplay feels very satisfying with you never relying too much on either. (unless you wanna challenge yourself with a no guns run which CAN be done.) the occult skills and the Madness system are an excellent replacement for my ancient enemy, the mana bar. 
Tombwater sounds incredible as well, relaxing, almost lonely guitar following you as you weave down city alleys, wander across desert plains, and trudge through haunted swaps. i got so lost in the music that the moments where the game takes it away feel very striking and tense. 
the Enemy designs are decently varied, but thankfully i've yet to run into and enemy that hours from now i'll re-encounter and go; 'ah yes. this asshole again.' 
I wont spoil the story but in trademark souls style, its sparse enough that it never feels like the game is beating you over the head with its narrative. which isn't to say its bad, just that you wont have to worry about sitting through huge text conversations if that's not your jam. 
and if you're thinking; this looks great but its probably too hard for me.' Tombwater has some great accessibility settings, so if you're like me and you want to explore rather than fight the same mobs over and over, you can tweak damage to give you an experience that's right for you. 
All in all, I love what Tombwater is doing and though its strange to say about a 2d game, its the best soulslike I've played in years. as soon as I finish this review, I'm booting it up again.
So far its a very fun game, it reminds me of bloodborne with its eldritch horror but it is also very different. I love the area design and enemies so far. Truly a fun game.

Okay, I'm only 5 hours and a bit into the game, but so far, I am having an absolute blast.

The combat feels great. It reminds me a bit of Hyper Light Drifter with having to balance dodging with shooting and melee attacks. I've only fought three bosses so far, but every move was well telegraphed, and once I got into the rhythm of the combat, it was satisfying.

The vibes are brilliant. The environments and enemies are interesting enough to me, to remind me of Fromsoft (more the eldritch horror stuff). The game also has the shortcuts and bonfire thing going on. But more than that, the music absolutely nails the eerie atmosphere. I'm enjoying it so much I ended up buying the soundtrack and the art book to support this dev.

It does have some difficulty, but if you're patient, and methodical about your movement and opportunities to attack, it's fine. I'm a fan of more difficult games so my bias might be present here. I've seen other reviews compare this to Zelda games and the like. I can't speak on that, but it does have that Bloodborne in the west vibe down quite well.

I don't really review games much at all, but I feel this game needs more eyes on it.

I'll likely update once I've finished the game, but for now, 5 hours in, I can wholeheartedly say given I didn't know much about this game beyond the trailer and bought it more or less on a whim, it's been absolutely worth it, and it's an easy recommendation.
Not a helpful review, but this game is awesome.
very good
Absolute Banger of a 2D souls game. Has every element right.
Nails the aesthetic. Good challenge. Exploration is rewarded.

It's like Hollow Knight progression meets Enter the Gungeon style combat, with all the right elements of subtle horror and ambience.  Very fun, very smooth, and overall a great game.  Highly recommend for those looking for a challenging, but rewarding,experience.
Spent a bunch of time in the demo along with the opening bits of the base game. Really solid blend of Soulslike and early Zelda. Has great feel and genuinely super solid map design.

El arte es bueno, la trama igual de buena.
En la demo, aprendí que debía temer los picos.
Ahora le temo más a las hachas y a las palas.

We are eating well this year, boys. First, we got Tearscape, and now we have Tombwater.  Tombwater is a great mix of Zelda with a Dark Tower/Bloodborne vibe.  The exploration and difficulty have been very enjoyable.  Hats off to the devs, y'all killed it. Now i long for more eldritch horror dark western media.

Big fan of the aesthetic; I love that the environment is quietly unsettling. Combat is satisfying and fair. I like the variety of weapons and spells I have found so far. Also a fan of leaning further into the eldritch setting for having spells having the madness level. I saw on some other reviews (other sites as well as here) about the controller aiming. I get where people are coming from, but I haven't  felt it is as a huge issue that its been made to be (in some cases). I'm a fan of the slow world building with each area being a distinct extension. The Wild West setting  is PERFECT, and I'm a huge fan of the weapons as a result. If you are on the fence, just give in. If you run out of bullets and a horse/cow monster is trying to murder you, be on brand, and brand it. BRAND IT GOOD

Aesthetics and Vibes? Incredible
Gameplay? Very fun
Plot? Intriguing enough

As a fan of the Weird West genre, this game nails a lot of what I love about it, while having some very fun progression and exploration. The boss fights can sometimes be frustrating - the game borrows heavily from SoulsBorne games in some of the boss fight design philosophy (in a good way) - but there's also some satisfaction to be found on beating one some of the harder fights. 
I think my only major complaint is the "platforming" of dashing across gaps - sometimes the gap is very close to the length of your dash and not very forgiving, so you need to be exclusively on the very edge of the gap to make the jump. However, falling down a pit does minimal damage, so that mitigates how bad it feels to miss a jump by pixels.

If you like westerns, horror, and fun gameplay then this is the game for you. If not then keep it pushing. The soundtrack is excellent. The controls is a little wonky but it works. The story is entertaining. It is really a great product that you can take a bite of and not want to have your stomach pumped.

First impression review: not played much but finding it fun. Reminds me of Hyperlight Drifter, but slower, not as cool looking, and not as well designed. I probably should’ve wishlisted and waited for a sale but the trailer drew me in and my impulsive nature took over. Happy to keep it in my library. I think people should try to switch up the soulslike genre.
Love this game - an excellent combination of visuals, mechanics, gameplay, and eldritch horror. Already have controller support was a huge plus for me as well.

Hey you! Yes, you! Do you like Bloodborne? Red Dead? How about Zelda? Well oh boy do I got a game for you! Tombwater exceeded my expectations and is a truly special experience that only comes around every so often. Do yourself a favor and get this game!

Tombwater takes me back to the days of the Super Nintendo, when games just felt different. This game is very set up like 'A link to the past' and that makes me love it even more. It does have some elements from different genres like soulslikes and metroidvanias, but I would still compare it most to Zelda.

This game was a lot higher quality than I was expecting going into it, and it has cemented itself as a game I will always come back to to the end of time. Exploration is very fun and the world feels very lived in and interesting, Combat is also a blast and the boss fights so far have been very well telegraphed and designed! I haven't beaten the game yet, but I'm honestly excited to see where the story is going and I cant wait to finish it! If I had to give a piece of criticism its that I wish there were costumes!

All in all, a solid 8.5 out of 10 Experience that keeps me coming back for more! Such an awesome game :)

This is such a fun game mixture. It's a Western styled Old School Zelda with Bloodborne inspirations.

It's challenging, but fair and the exploration and discovery (opening up shortcuts and finding secrets) has a great pace to it. Definitely gives a retro feel and I have been loving it so far!

This game is awesome, a real Stephen King gunslinger feeling with the game play of a Dark Souls (In 2D of course), great sound track, A good challenge.  Highly recommend and I have only played an hour or so.

Only a couple of hours in, but holy shit this is a banger. 

Really good world building, beautiful environments and oh my God the music. It's nothing super elaborate but it's so good. 

The gameplay is really solid as well, it's simple but with much more depth than it seems. This really feels like a love letter to the OG soulslikes, all the staples of the genres are there, but in a way that made me smile, not one that felt derivative. The game really channels that "Bloodborne in the old west" vibe but in a way that's compelling and makes sense for the setting, it doesn't feel like a ripoff at all. 

Again, the world building really feels like it has a lot of effort put into it - the item description, weapon descriptions, environments, dialogues, etc.

The enemy design definitely deserves a mention because there were some cool ones. 

I haven't been this excited to get back home to play a game in a while. 

Don't sleep on this!
love the style, mechanics are simple but have enough depth that there are endless possibilites in combat. Already love it.

Switching to negative as my original compromise with the devs made no sense on further examination (see drama in comments and dev response). This wasn't a misunderstanding by a small team with good intents, this is likely a lazy cash grab. I'll explain: 

The reason the aiming and movement feels off is because they used an engine not built for this kind of game, probably purposely. So then the devs claim adding aim assist or more/better controller controls and options wouldn't be possible with the Solarus engine. Hell, many of the issues with the game stem from there. So you'd think that they must have needed to use this engine then, right?

Nope. Godot is free and light as well while being actaully feature rich. They could have used it like many better indie devs have and is usually the indie dev standard for 2d games. Solarus (I believe made by one guy) is meant for quick small project 2D zelda clones that are usually free (think Yarntown), that's why they can't fix the aiming issues. It was never meant for a fast paced combat heavy game (yes Zelda games have combat but it's usually very limited on the 2d titles).

Hell, Tearscape (which released right before this) is an actual 2D Zelda mechanically and is also mixed with Bloodbourne (and a much better game while being $10 cheaper), used Godot. It could have used Solarus more justifiably but the dev actually cared about his vision and wanted to build the game fully.

My guess is the Tombwater devs either couldn't figure out how to build their game genuinely from scratch or didn't want to put in the work, so they basically used a free template, copied Yarntown but added cowboys, then charged $25 and blame the customers/engine/steam for its shortcomings. 

Hell, probably the reason the aiming and controls don't feel intentional is that those were the default options in the engine and the devs just said "good enough". The game is like one or two steps removed from an asset flip. This compounded with them just letting steam put "controller recommended" on the page since that probably leads to more steam deck sales; until I called them out and they removed it.

Which sucks because this could have been the spiritual Yarntown sequel or 2D Bloodbourne we always wanted, but it's clearly a cash grab. Make this game like $5 and sure, it's "good enough". Charging as much or more than some of best indie games of all time is laughable.

I feel bad for the artists though as that seems to be the only thing that was done with any true artistic intent.
reviews.developer_response:
Hi there Rektnarok! Thank you for playing the game, caring enough about it to leave feedback, and for being open to discussion about the parts you're not happy with.

We personally feel that the description of 'controller fully supported' is fair to apply to this game. Usually 'partial support' refers to games where major features simply cannot be done on controller at all-- which is not true in this case! Everything in the game runs well on controller and Steam Deck. We also provided alternate aim options and control remapping to as much of a degree as the Solarus engine would allow.

However, it's understandable that the 'twin stick' playstyle can sometimes be difficult/is not everyone's preference. We hear you that you'd prefer there to be some sort of aim assist.

Developing something like an aim assist toggle would take time, and investigation to evaluate whether it's in the cards to implement. In the meantime, I think the best we can offer is to adjust the Steam Storefront settings to "Controller Supported" rather than "Controller Recommended".

Honestly, the "Controller Recommended" setting was kind of a holdover from earlier demo builds where the M/KB control scheme was not fully polished, anyway. It was an attempt to encourage folks to use the more polished control scheme instead-- but now, it's just a matter of preference.

Would that change help address your concerns?

reviews.review: About 2 hours in and can already tell this is pretty good. It's the old west meets bloodborne and I am for it.
great game, difficult. games with demos very nice
Geniunely some of the most fun ive had but also some of the navigation and fights pissed me off. Still a really solid game. ALSO JUMPSCARES I GUESS?
Only an hour in, but having a blast.
2 hours in and pleasantly surprised by the quality of this game: smooth gameplay, thoughtful puzzles, detailed enemies requiring strategic assessment, cool ambience and music. A must play!

Controller and Deck both work fine. Top negative review has apparently never played a twin stick shooter before. Or maybe just the ones that do the aiming for you. "Feels like it's built for mouse...needs auto-aim or lock on". No, it doesn't. This kind of controller aiming has been a thing for a long time without needing the game to target stuff for you. Learn to aim. 

Game is a top down Old West inspired Souls-like that takes more inspiration from Bloodborne with it's mythos and mechanics. You wield a main weapon which can vary between fast/short range daggers, long swords or slower axes/clubs. Secondary weapon is a gun which can be your standard single shot pistol or multi-shot shotgun (perhaps others I haven't found yet). Weapons can also have various effects on them like poison or faster bullet recovery. Speaking of bullets, you have a set amount (6 to start) and weapons take a certain number of bullets when you fire (1 for pistol, 2 for shotgun) and you recover shots as you do melee damage. So you'll unload your shots (which do considerable damage) and swap to melee to recover. There's also spells that do things like throw fire, do a howl to stun/knock back enemies or do the blood bullet thing from Bloodborne. Using these options builds up "madness" which is similar to frenzy in Elden Ring. The meter empties on it's own (or with items) but if you cast too much it'll max out and you can no longer cast until resting. There's also sub items that can heal, buff or be thrown to do damage/debuffs to enemies. Crafted item like grenades are automatically recharged at campfires just like your healing flask. 

Enemies early on consist of ye ol' miners and cowboys with the occasional cthulu inspired montrosity. Some do melee combos, others take pot shots at you (sometimes in between melee attacks) and other just want to punch the world. I've faced a few bosses so far and none have been especially challenging. I don't think I've died more than once or twice to any of them. 

Plenty of paths that loop back on itself, shortcuts and even some fake walls to discover. They do tend to stand out just enough to notice if you're paying attention and overlook them if you're not. 

The music is nice and fitting for the setting. Nothing standout so far but it's enjoyable to listen to while exploring around. The story is interesting enough without getting in the way. I'm curious about where it's going and what led to the cthulu outbreak. 

As for negatives, they come down to a couple things that aren't too big a deal. First is the controls. They work fine out the box but holding L2 to bring up your gun is awkward when you have to aim with right stick. It can be changed to just aim in the direction of the right stick but ONLY in game, not from the main menu. There's also the option to just aim in the direction you're looking if that's your thing. Devs really need to put this in the main menu. 

Another negative is that enemy AI needs a bit of tuning. They can't go up stairs (it seems) and will get caught on the terrain when moving towards you (meaning they'll just keep moving into that lamp and not go around it). You can easily abuse this to take out tougher enemies. 

My final negative is that an aspect of stats isn't explained before picking your starting class. You actually CAN NOT level up most stats like in your typical souls-like; just life, stamina and lucidity (essentially mana). So your starting class actually matters a bit. If you pick a melee focused starter, your offensive stats are going to be based around that. It doesn't mean you can't do other combat options just that it might not be as effective as if you chose one focused on that playstyle. If this changes later in the game then cool beans but nothing in the earlier parts hints at this being possible. 

The game is quite enjoyable and there's a demo! Give it a try. It consists of the intro section and then jumps ahead a bit into the game.

So far ive only played 2 hours of the full release and i can tell you that those 2 hours are in my top 10 moments of all time. this game is incredible ad ive never played anything quite like it: the combinations of wildwest, soulslike and zelda like perspective realy just makes it so diffrent. i love this game.

Something about the twang of an old west ballad combined with the deep rot of eldritch madness makes the initial impression of this game very interesting. Something tells me I won't like what I find in the dark, and yet I have the desire to venture deeper to find out what it is.
